utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. We are back after so many days now, so we will try and carry on from where we had stopped. Before we start the proceedings of this morning, I think we will try to deal with two outstanding motions. The first one is the prosecution's intention to show video excerpts to Witness N. We think we should clear that up before we continue with the witness. The second one is a video link as well. I think we can clear these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have one -- concerning this matter, pursuant to Rule 54, I have one request concerning point two, the request for the inclusion of the transcript of the audio-visual recordings that the Prosecutor handed over in March and the admissibility of evidence, point two in your order. I would request, your Honour, that we have that hearing after we have heard Witness I, that is I want to ask your permission to have this discussion when we have finished with Witness N and Miro Golubovic and with Witness I. The motive for this request is the flexibility of the witnesses. They are waiting to appear before the court, and therefore I think we could without harming anybody's interest have this discussion after having heard these witnesses, your Honour. That is my request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Do you think the motions we have before us have anything to do with this matter, with what you have raised?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Just a question of timing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Let us get what you have raised out of our chest and then we can take up whatever you are now raising.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Instead of bringing it in between what we are doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Okay. We can take it up when it arises after we have dealt with point one. Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Now who is speaking to the motion? It is the prosecution's motion. Who is speaking to it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you want me to start with the first issue, which is the showing of an excerpt videotape to Witness N, we have actually filed a short motion on that, asking for the showing of this excerpt video link to Witness N. We had already a response from one of the defence parties, MR. Delic's defence lawyers. We understand that he would not object to that, provided we are not going to have the sound audible in this court room, and we certainly assure you that the idea of the prosecution is showing only the excerpt video without any sound in order to have the witness recognise places and persons and nothing else, and after that there would be from the part of the prosecution let us say provisional exhibiting of this excerpt video, which might become definitive after the final exhibiting of the original seized videotape. This is the sense of our request, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Any impression on the part of the defence? MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, proceeding from the argument presented by the distinguished prosecution representative at the last sitting and what has been said today, the defence of Zejnil Delalic is opposed to the use and showing of the videotape to Witness N; namely, as noted by the prosecution, it is an excerpt of an allegedly seized tape found on the accused. The prosecution has proposed on the list of his witnesses an Austrian policeman as a witness, who has to state before this Trial Chamber whether this is seized material, first, and, secondly, whether this material was lawfully seized. Both facts are essential for a just trial and are in the interest of justice. Explaining his request, the prosecution referred to economical reasons, but these cannot precede the interests of legality, fairness and justice. My client has reason to claim that the evidence taken by the prosecution is not evidence whose validity can be established at this Trial Chamber, therefore, before it is established that the prosecution has evidence in his possession that has been obtained lawfully, for that evidence to be shown to witnesses. Thank you, your Honours. MS. TAPUSKOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honour, referring to the motion of the prosecution to show this videotape, we must point out that it should be underlined that this cassette is a compilation of extracts taken from the apartment of the accused, Mr. Mucic, and we join in what my learned colleague, Ms Residovic, said, that this evidence may be shown only after the witness is heard who first found that tape, and he is number 35 on the prosecution's list. Regardless of the allegations made by the prosecution now, that if the Trial Chamber allows the presentation of this tape, the sound would be switched off and only the pictures would be shown to the witness in order to identify certain persons in the Celebici camp, we still allege that when the witness number 35 on the list appears, that is a member of the Austrian police, I would ask your Honours to allow us to reserve the right to discuss this question again, whether the sound can also be used for the tape. Therefore, the arguments should be made then against the use of this tape with the sound. If the prosecution feels that we should present arguments now, we may do so. There is no problem on our side. We can do that now, but otherwise we feel that this videotape prepared by the prosecution could be shown only after the appearance of witness number 35. I apologise. I do not recall his name. It is a German name. Only then can we discuss whether such evidence is acceptable, and I support all that has been said by my learned colleague Ms Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honours, on behalf of Defendant Esad Landzo, we, having not participated and not owned the videotapes, have no standing to contest the legality of the seizure. So we defer to our esteemed colleagues representing Mr. Delalic and Mr. Mucic on those areas. As far as the content of the videotape itself being shown for identification purposes only, we have no objections to that part as long as, of course, the tapes were legally seized according to the other two defendants, and as long as there is no audiotape. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so that the record is clear, Mr. Delic has no objection to the admission of the video. We have not agreed to the admission of the audio, not just that it would not be played. We do not agree to the admissibility of it. I think that is the agreement we have with the prosecution, that the audio, the words, would, in fact, not be introduced into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually if I understand the contention of the prosecution, at this stage all they want are just excerpts of the video itself, not the entire document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That is correct, your Honour. With that entire understanding, that the audio is not even introduced, we have no objection to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: So it is not admitting the video into evidence, just identifying excerpts for purposes of admission?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That is correct, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think this is all they are trying to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your Honour, have I understood in your statement we only show the video without even a provision of exhibiting?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Well, you want to make it an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Well, let us say -- I will repeat that we are quite in agreement with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: You have to show how it can be an exhibit under this witness, who is merely identifying certain excerpts in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The prosecution is very flexible on that. We might simply have in the record of the testimony the witness recognising places and persons and nothing else. If the provisional exhibiting of the tape itself is not deemed to be necessary anyway for reasons of the record, but anyway, even in case of a provisional exhibiting, in our submission, that would be provisional in the sense that it might become definitive only when we will be in a position to prove the legal seizure of the tape and then reach the admission of the original seized tape as a definitive exhibit. Anyway our position is quite flexible. We reassure the defence lawyers that we are not going to play the audio of this videotape, and we simply would like to have the witness recognise persons whenever he is in a position to do that, and if there is no objection to this kind of a provisional exhibiting, we will be happy to do that. Otherwise we will not even try to have this kind of a provisional exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I wish I understood all you have said, because all you are trying to show is that this witness identifies certain persons in the video? This is all you say. It makes no claim as to how the video was produced. He has no authority as to how it came into possession. I do not see how you can even bring it into exhibiting at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right, your Honour. I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You want to identify them at a particular place or a particular time? Why do you want to get them identified? The witness knows the accused persons. So why do you want this identification? For what purpose? I just want information, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The idea is to have the witness recognising and identifying people inside the camp, the same way we did in one of the past hearings with an excerpt video of the same tape, I think, which defence counsels wanted to show to some witnesses for the same reason. This is all what we ask to do. In that case there was anyway an exhibiting of the excerpt video shown to the witnesses, but in our submission this does not make much difference to the prosecution. So we could even be happy in simply having the witness watch the tape and say whether he recognises any person and nothing else, and we might not even have this kind of a provisional exhibit, which I understand the Chamber is sceptical about. I hope my explanation was sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: We are still in the process of argument. Let us hear -- Ms Residovic wanted to say something. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you, your Honours. If the prosecution wishes the witness to identify places and persons, he has already provided evidence for the court, the model of the camp, the plan, and the photo-spread, and he could have done that for certain persons in this way. The explanation that the defence also used a videotape for purposes of identification I think is not acceptable, since this was a cross-examination by the defence and, secondly, the prosecution has the authority to be able to prove that certain pieces of evidence are legally in his possession before presenting it to the Trial Chamber. MS. TAPUSKOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, in addition to what colleague Residovic has said, that the prosecution was able to carry out the identification in other ways of the camp using the model and the photo-spread and videotapes, the motion of the prosecution of 10th April to allow such evidence in the course of the hearing of Witness N. We were also supplied with a transcript of those excerpts, which are part of the compilation of the videotape which the prosecution wishes to show. We see from the transcript that, with the exception of one of the accused, among the persons shown on the tape there are no other accused, not a single witness, nor any of the guards that are familiar to the participants in these proceedings. What the prosecution wishes to achieve is the question; with the introduction of this videotape the identification of which persons? I would like them to answer this question. Do they wish to combine the accused with third persons, the guards or anyone else? I see no legal relevance of identifying persons and, according to the transcript of the audiotape we were supplied with by the prosecution, regardless of the fact that the prosecution is now stating that for the moment it has no intention of using the audio. Therefore, we need to have proof of the legal relevance of the introduction of such evidence, because we do not know which persons the prosecution wants to be identified.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might add just one more point just for clarification, the videotape excerpts that have been played before were on cross-examination and were solely --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO BENITO
utterances.text: Could you wait, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Oh, I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes? Let us hear you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: The videotape before was solely used for cross-examination purposes limited to the purpose of impeachment of a prosecution witness. At this point the prosecution is now putting on its case in chief, which means they are presenting evidence in the case, which I think is the clear difference between playing the videotape before and offering the videotape at this time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think we will later give our reasons in full, but I think after listening to the arguments the Trial Chamber is convinced that it is not really necessary for any identification of any person through the excerpts of these videos before they come into evidence. It is not necessary. The next motion is one from the prosecution also to allow witnesses K, L and M to give their testimony by means of videolink conference. So who is speaking to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I will do that briefly again. We filed this kind of a motion because the two witnesses L and K, have serious medical reasons which prevent them from coming to The Hague concerning the lady and the son of both witnesses. We maintain this request for a videolink for these two witnesses. On the other hand, we withdraw now the request concerning witness M, because, concerning witness M, the host country gave assurances that he will be readmitted into the host country after the testimony. So we maintain our request concerning witnesses K and L and withdraw it concerning Mr. M. As for the reasons why we requested this kind of protective measures for these witnesses, now with these two witnesses, I cannot say -- I would not add anything than what is already written in our motion, your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Can we hear the defence on this? Any reaction?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we made clear in our written response so long as the prosecution complies with the decision from the Tadic Trial Chamber on the procedural requirements and logistical requirements and setting things up, Mr. Delic would have no objection at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Any other ...?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Esad Landzo does object to the videolink testimony of these witnesses as, pursuant to Article 21 of the Rights of the Accused, 21.4(e), and I believe Rule 89 of the Rules of Evidence, he has a right to have the witnesses present in the court room to testify. I do not believe that we have sufficient evidence that these medical reasons of children or siblings or whatever it is that they have presented represent sufficient reason for them not to be presented here in the court room. So the rights of the accused to confront the accusers in person in the court room, I believe, would be violated as far as Esad Landzo is concerned. We do not object to any other protections as long as the witness himself is present in the court room. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would respectfully concur with my learned friend who has just spoken on that subject. Thank you. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, the defence of Zejnil Delalic also is on the position that the witness needs to present his testimony confronting the accused. However, we do accept that in certain situations, which need to be reasoned in detail and under very strict conditions, as in the Tadic case, at the Prosecutor's as well as the defence request, there could be some exceptions and the testimony could be provided through videolink. In this specific case, though, we do not see that the prosecution has offered good enough reasons. How, it is our position that, should the Trial Chamber accept this motion in this or any future cases, an issue needs to be resolved which is of some significance for the defence; in other words, how can a witness be provided with some piece of evidence which the defence might want to use in order to impeach the witness or want to use in any other way? The Delalic defence also wants to point out another reason. We will submit in writing to this Trial Chamber that some witnesses have been under a significant influence of the Association of Detainees. This Association has requested before the beginning of this trial that defence get no contact with the witnesses and that it is exerting strong influence on the witnesses. Our learned colleague, Ms McHenry, also pointed out that the Prosecutor does not always have direct contact with the witnesses, but that it gets in touch with the witnesses sometimes through the Association of Detainees. Therefore, the Delalic defence submits that if the videolink is used, the location where this videolink is coming from also needs a person, a representative from both prosecution and defence present at that location. Thank you, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Turone, do you want to add anything? You can take a question from my brother judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I do not know; I am not really asking you to make any predictions but how long do you think you will take in concluding your evidence? A month, two months, six weeks, how long?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You mean the whole prosecution case?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: That is a good question, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: As I said, I do not want you to make any exact predictions. This has a bearing on the motion for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: A couple of months. Maybe a couple of months.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Two months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I add something else on this issue, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, please. Let us hear you in reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: First of all, if there is simply a matter of evidence, we are ready to prepare some affidavits and enter some documentation concerning the medical reasons of Ms. and Mrs. -- Mr. and Mrs. K and L, if this is simply a matter of evidence. On the other hand, I do not know if this is very useful for our esteemed colleagues of the defence lawyers, but we not only have no information that this association is improperly behaving, but anyway these two specific witnesses, K and L, had no contact with this association, because they are in a host country and they were not anyway contacted by us through this association. Anyway, the real point I wanted to point out, there is a matter of sufficient evidence. We are ready to prepare -- have some affidavits and documentation on the medical situation concerning these two witnesses and their son. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Perhaps before you sit down, I think what really bothers us is the point which has been made by some defence counsel that a videolink conference by itself is in violation of Article 21(e). I thought that is what you should have directed your attention to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we rely upon the case law in the Tadic case. Of course, this measure has to be a very, very exceptional measure, and in the Tadic case that was stated, but since it was admitted in the Tadic case under very strict conditions, we supposed -- in our submission we think this might be anyway ruled in other very exceptional circumstances like that. On the other hand, the videolink can be done with particular careful measures so as to respond to every single requirement belonging to the right of correct cross-examination and rights of the defence in general. Of course, this needs some specific practical measures which were anyway taken, as far as I know, in the Tadic case. This is all I can -- this is what I can say about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I asked you that question about the estimate you will take, because I had something in my mind. You do not have to produce those witnesses immediately. Wait for a month and a half. You will not conclude your evidence before that. Maybe the health of the relatives of these two witnesses will have improved by that time and they are in a position to come. We will consider that question at that stage. This is what I have in mind. That is why I asked you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: This is anyway the other side of my views on the proper evidence on this specific situation, because the medical situation of these two persons is not a medical situation which can really change better in a couple of months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: We are not doing that, but there are some particular medical situations, health situations, because of -- I do not know -- heavy cancer or other very, very grave illnesses which probably in any state of the world can be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Why not wait and examine them later?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone please, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: If they are still unable to come, you can repeat your request.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right. That might be also ....

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think we have heard you. I think you are not entitled to tell the prognosis at this stage. We will know what to do. We will come back in 30 minutes time and give you a ruling. (10.45 am) (Short break) (11.25 am)

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know that the court has been deliberating on this issue to give us a ruling on the prosecution's motion at this moment, but the defence attorneys have had a discussion in the defence room and we have a little further argument to offer in relation to this issue of videolink testimony, if the court would so entertain. If not, we will be forced to file our own motion and reopen this issue at another time. So whichever way you would like to hear it. It is relevant to the issue before the court, but if you would rather hear our arguments at another time, we will file a further motion and ask for another hearing on this motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: You assume too many things. You think merely because you file a further motion, you get it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: We hope so, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Do not make your own rulings before you hear them. Nobody ever makes rulings when you are asking somebody else for his decision. You have made up your mind. You have to make further applications and get it reargued on your own terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am sorry if I presented the question improperly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: As you have always done. In any event, if it is necessary to put on further arguments, the Trial Chamber will hear that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: We are supposed to hear these things.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: So I have permission to go into it now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: If it is the decision of the defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Mme Residovic had already mentioned this issue before about the evidence that we have that there has been some -- I hate to use this term; I am afraid to -- possible tampering of the witnesses and not by the prosecution. We are not alleging that any member of this Tribunal has had any kind of contact with the witnesses that has been improper. That is not the allegation of the defence at all. But we believe that there is a foreign group which has been soliciting testimony and prompting these witnesses, and under its -- it is in violation of Rule 90(d) of the Statute of this Tribunal as construed by the Trial Chamber in the Prosecution v Tadic. That decision was number IT-94-1-T. It is about preventing the contamination of witnesses in the case, whether it is for the prosecution or for the defence. We would like to bring to the court's attention, and I have provided the prosecution with two articles that have been in the clipping service provided to us by the Tribunal. One of the articles -- we have the English translation of it too. We will provide that to the court after the prosecution gets through looking at it. One of the articles is by -- The Congress of the Serb Unity and Association of the Camp Prisoners warn the Celebici victims. It says: "Stay away from lawyers." It is dated May 25th, 1996, this article. I will present the whole article to the court in a moment. There is another article, which is the newest article -- do you have it, Tom? I have it. I am sorry, your Honours. It is dated March 30th, 1997. It comes from the newspaper clipping from the Belgrade Daily newspaper. It talks about the testimony of Grosdana Cecez and the testimony of Mirko Babic, and it also talks about a counsellor named Slobodan Stojanovic, who represents the Serbian witnesses, victims for the International Tribunal, and how he coaches them, how he talks to them, and further I think taints their testimony in a way that has yet to be proven, but I believe if we could have these people come forward -- they may even be in the court room today. The edition of the Belgrade Evening News talks about a Serbian attorney, Slobodan Stojanovic, who discussed the testimony of Grosdana Cecez and Mirko Babic. In that story Mr. Stojanovic says that they did not tell half the story that they knew because they were too embarrassed or because they did not feel like it was worth repeating. Additionally, on April 18th, 1997, which is from our press clippings from the Tribunal, the Information Office translated the Editiona Politika, which is a story that quotes Dusika Bojic, the Secretary of the Association of Detainees, discussing the testimony of Witness N and Milojka Antic. In the article Mr. Bojic is quoted as saying Witness N is the Association's key witness. Mr. Bojic is further quoted as stating that Witness N went through terrible tortures, and he further indicates that he had access to the witness statements of other witnesses who placed Ms. Antic in Celebici. Rule 90(d) is being violated by persons unconnected with the Office of the Prosecutor or the Tribunal informing witnesses of the contents of prior witness statements. It also is possible that someone outside the Tribunal is preparing the witnesses for their testimony and helping them shade their testimony or even commit perjury. The Association of Detainees now claim that their witnesses have told the OTP in their written statements and they are alleging that they have had testimony to statements that nobody else has had access to. Also, if you look back on the testimony of Mirko Babic and Ms. Cecez, a lot of it seemed memorised. When asked outside her direct testimony about questions, she would say she did not remember or did not recall. It was very difficult for either one of them to depart from the script. Anyway, we feel that also they have had discussions with Ms. Cecez and then discussed Ms. Cecez's testimony with Ms. Antic, because she was well aware that the defence had access to the medical records and had time to prepare for that testimony coming up. We are certainly not laying any suspicion on the prosecution whatsoever, but we ask this court to take into consideration the fact that by videolink testimony, we have no access to these witnesses, that the Association of Serbian witnesses has now told all the witnesses not to talk to the defence attorneys and also that because of the probability, the high probability, with this association of tampering with the witnesses in some sort, we feel it more desirable, and of course under Rule 21.4(e) the rights of the accused would be better preserved, if we could also have the witnesses present in the court room. We ask that this court conduct a hearing into this matter to make sure that each witness knows that they are not supposed to be coached by any outside sources; they are not supposed to get information other than their own personal knowledge about their testimony in the court room, and if the court adopts that Tadic decision, then each witness should be given some kind of document telling them what it is that their conduct is expected in this court room. I would like to introduce both of these articles to the court for your consideration on this matter. They have been interpreted. The prosecution has the original documents over there, but we would like to have both marked as defence exhibits and presented to the court. I believe my learned colleague Mme Residovic may have a few more words to add to this argument, but we would like the court to please conduct an investigation into this area also. That is one of our main reasons why we think the videolink testimony is not appropriate in this trial. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms Residovic. Can we hear you? MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): My learned colleague, Ms McMurrey, has presented all the arguments on behalf of the defence. Presenting our views regarding the videolink, I had these arguments in mind, and we thought that it was necessary for the Trial Chamber to hear these arguments in much greater detail as they were presented by Ms McMurrey. We feel that this is in the interests of a fair trial. As I said at the beginning, when I spoke as defence counsel for Zejnil Delalic, anything that might impair the fairness of the trial in this Tribunal we will be focussing on, and we will appeal to the Trial Chamber to hear our arguments and to pass a ruling in that sense. The defence of Zejnil Delalic concurs fully with the statements of the defence of Mr. Landzo.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, outside of this, we have one more request too, that since Witness N has been described by this organisation as their key witness, who has been prompted, that perhaps we could have a voir dire examination of Witness N to determine whether or to what extent he has visited with people outside of the Office of the Prosecutor and outside of this Tribunal. Thank you: if I might have the usher, I will offer these articles to the court for their consideration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think we will read them later. I do not know what useful purpose it will serve at this stage. We have heard all the arguments. Do you want to make any replies?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, just briefly. It is not entirely clear to me how any of this is relevant to videolink testimony, since videolink testimony occurs under the direction of the court and there are people from the Registry handling it. So we, in fact, do not see the relevance of this. It seems more a closing argument. With respect to the particular issues, there is -- as far as I can tell, there is nothing in those articles which suggests that the witnesses have been discussing their testimony with other witnesses or that they are being coached or tailored. We certainly do not believe that there is any evidence before this court either from their own -- from how the witnesses appeared or even when the defence has attempted to get into this on cross-examination. The association, as I understand it, is not a -- it is certainly not a part of the Tribunal, but it is a voluntary association that certain witnesses have chosen to belong to. I do not believe it is within this court's -- not authority, but I do not believe there is any need for this court to get into what they have done. The issue is: are the witnesses telling the truth? Has anyone told them what to say? I can assure the court that the Association does not have access to any Office of the Prosecutor's statements and any statements being referred to would be separate ones, which we believe in some instances there are and have been given to the defence. So, your Honours, we do not believe that there is anything suggesting that anything improper has happened with respect to any of the witnesses, and, as far as the allegation that an organisation in the US may have advised witnesses to not speak with defence attorneys, again that is certainly the office of -- I think it is agreed that the Office of the Prosecutor has never done that, but if an association decides to give advice, I think it is up to the witness to take it or not take it, but I do not believe that there is anything per se improper in doing that. So your Honours can look at the articles, but when the prosecution has briefly looked at them, we have not seen any evidence that anything that has gone on before this court -- that the witnesses have behaved improperly or that there has been any violation whatsoever of any of the court's -- the Tribunal's rules, including Rule 90. I certainly believe the defence has and in appropriate circumstances can continue to cross-examine on that issue, but I do not believe anything further is required.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I am very grateful for the assistance of all counsel in these applications. Fortunately this is not the first time an application of this nature has been presented and I think it is necessary to understand that this Trial Chamber will protect the interests of both the accused persons, the witnesses and the prosecution also. It is an impartial Trial Chamber, as the Tribunal is, and in coming to our decision we have taken particular care to ensure that none of the rights of the accused persons is affected by the measure we adopt. Now possibly there might be some misunderstanding of the nature of the videolink conference. The Registry of this Tribunal is fully in charge of the videolink conference even outside the Trial Chamber here. A member of the Registry will be sent abroad and will conduct the examination and the arrangement for the videolink conference. For whatever it may mean, there is the assurance that the organisation will be perfect and counsel will be able to cross-examine, see the accused persons in the videolink, and the Trial Chamber will be sitting to determine the nature of the examination of the witnesses. Now, the argument about witness tampering, that might be quite new. I would not know. Perhaps prosecution might also not know. Referring the Trial Chamber into instituting an inquiry into that is unnecessarily expanding our own horizon. Unless there is sufficient evidence to show that any such thing is going on and not that any meddlesome internal person is doing that, there cannot be made out. In the present circumstances of the conflict going on anything can happen and one does not rely on much of the information which is being dished out from all corners. As far as we are concerned, we are more interested in the motion before us and we deal with it in accordance with the Rules and the Statutes of this court, of this Trial Chamber I mean. Now, the main argument has been that it is a violation of Article 21.4(e). We do not think that is correct, because the accused persons have all opportunities to cross-examine and examine the witnesses and the Trial Chamber also has an opportunity of observing the demeanour of the witnesses. So no provision is violated. For the inconvenience which might be suggested, we have looked into it and we have come to the conclusion that this is not outweighed by the benefit that might arise from protecting the witnesses and the interest involved. So we agree with the prosecution application that a video conference will be organised for K and L. M, who was formerly included in the whole arrangement, the prosecution has withdrawn its application, because the circumstances are no longer the same. We grant the application to issue the video conference. The Registry will be informed to proceed accordingly. Now, before we conclude this aspect, I have to apologise, because my familiarity with this body is breeding a little contempt in that I did not ask for representation when we started. Counsel did not announce their presence, both the prosecution and the defence. I assume we have all been the same. I appeal to everybody to forgive and kindly announce their presence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. I will do that. I am Eric Ostberg and I am accompanied in this trial by my learned colleagues Mr. Giuliano Turone, Mrs. Teresa McHenry and our case manager, Ms. Elles van Dusschoten. Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Can we now hear the defence? MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): My name is Edina Residovic, defence counsel of Zejnil Delalic. With me is my colleague, Eugene O'Sullivan, Professor of Criminal Law, and our colleague, Ekrem Galijatovic, will not be participating for a time in the hearings in this Trial Chamber, and we will announce his repeated appearance in due time to the court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am Michael Greaves. I appear on behalf of the defendant Mucic, and I am assisted today by Mrs. Mira Tapuskovic, who appears as my legal assistant in this case. He is also represented by Mr. Branoslav Tapuskovic, who is lead counsel in the case, but who is not present in court at the present time. MR. KARABDIC (in interpretation): My name is Salih Karabdic, defence counsel of the accused Mr. Hazim Delic. With me in the team is Mr. Tom Moran, lawyer from Houston, Texas. MR. BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): Good morning, your Honours. My name is Mustafa Brackovic, attorney from Sarajevo, defending the accused Esad Landzo, together with my learned colleague, Cynthia McMurrey, from the United States. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I am happy that you accept my apology for that. We can now continue with our last witness and I think break in about an hour's time. Can we have the witness? Witness N (continued)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Would you kindly swear the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I wish to remind you that you are still testifying under oath.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I proceed, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. So, Mr. N, last time you told us something about your valuables having been taken from you. Now my question is: did you ever get your property back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (In interpretation): no.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Would the witness please move closer to the microphone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never received my property back.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. My next and I would say last question now. For the convenience of the Chamber and the defence lawyers I am referring to the transcript on page 1914. When I asked the witness: "Do you remember approximately when you saw Mr. Mucic for the first time?", you answered: "I don't know the exact date." Now my question is: do you remember roughly in which month you saw Mr. Mucic for the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly which month it could have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right, your Honour. My examination-in-chief is finished. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Turone. Has the defence decided the order of their cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. We will proceed in the following way. First, counsel for Mr. Mucic; second, counsel for Mr. Delic; third, counsel for Mr. Landzo; and, fourth, counsel for Mr. Delalic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Greaves, you can now take the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I am reminded to ask that the screen is preventing Mr. Mucic from seeing the witness giving his evidence. I would ask that he be able to do that please. Perhaps your court usher can just make a slight adjustment to make sure that he can see him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: On the right side.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: It may be if I use the podium it will be simpler. It is extremely loud and I have got a terrible echo in my ... thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: You can control the sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. N, I want to ask you, first of all, please, about the two interrogations which were carried out with you at Celebici camp, about which you told us when you were here some time ago. Do you remember giving evidence about those two interviews?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The first of those two interviews was carried out by a man you told us Mladen Zovko; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first was by Mladen -- the first interrogation was by Mladen Zovko.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The second interrogation was carried out just prior to your release by Pavo Mucic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It was roughly some time in August. After that I was transferred to another prison, to the sports hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I am sorry. You are quite right. It was before your transfer to the sports hall, the point I make is this: the interrogation by Mr. Mucic, that was just before you were moved from Celebici to the other camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you. You have cleared up the bad question that I asked and I apologise for asking it badly, Mr. N. The two interrogations, Mr. N, would it be right to say that they were quite different in their nature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly whether they were different.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Can I help you about this: the interview that you had with Mr. Mucic, would you accept that that was a very short interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was short.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Just two or three very quick questions being written down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were several questions. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: But that interview was very much shorter than the one that had been conducted by Mladen Zovko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The interview with Mladen Zovko, was that an unpleasant experience for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When Mladen Zovko interrogated me, I had before that been beaten up, so I can't remember very well what he asked me even.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did it last for a long time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe roughly about an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The interview with Mr. Mucic lasted how long?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe about 20 minutes or half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I want to ask you this question now, and it is the last one that I am going to ask you, Mr. N: it is right, is it not, that some time during your stay in Celebici you heard that Pavo Mucic had issued orders that no one should be beaten. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard of that, but I personally was beaten up after those orders. I heard one of the guards say that orders had come after the International Red Cross visit that nobody should beat us, but I was beaten by Kemal Mr.dzic, a guard, and Samir Honda.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: That may well be so, but the point is this, is it not, that you heard that Pavo Mucic had issued such orders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Moran?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can get a second to be situated with earphones and things ... may it please the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can take the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. N.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: My name is Tom Moran and, as I am sure you noticed, I represent Hazim Delic in this case. I am going to ask you some questions and if you do not understand one of them, will you stop me and ask me to explain it or break it down, or whatever it takes, so you understand the question that is asked; will you do that for me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Would you just answer the question that I ask? Some of them may just call for a "yes" or "no". Could you just answer those with just "yes" or "no"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. First thing I would like to talk about is: you arrived in Celebici on May 23rd; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: You were taken to Hangar 22?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That was the day that your property was taken; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So it was the evening of 23rd May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: All right. You did not see Mr. Delic there at that time, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. Let us go on to another subject. Let us talk a little bit about the death of Scepo Gotovac; okay? As I recall when you testified here last week, you testified that when he was brought back into the hangar that he had some kind of a badge nailed to his head; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And you testified at that time that you did not recall whether it was an SDA badge or an SDS badge; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: If I showed you an SDA badge, would you recognise one of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: If the usher could show him one, I have one in my pocket.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I thought he said "no".

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That is fine, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I did not know whether I would be able to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, whatever pleases the court. If I can show it to him, I have it. If it would not be helpful, that is fine too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Well, it depends on you, because from his answers -- it depends what you think you can get out of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the usher could show it to him. We can mark it, if the court desires, and put it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: As what? (Badge handed to witness).

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Is that the kind of badge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know if this is the one that was there. There must be different kinds of badges.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. Do you remember talking to the investigators from the Office of the Prosecutor on February 23rd and 24th 1996 about that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: You can return his badge to him.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone please, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: But you remember meeting with the Office of the Prosecutor back in February of 1996. There was an investigator there and an interpreter there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Was there anyone present during the interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Do you remember at that time you told them that it was an SDS Bosnian-Serb political party badge that was nailed to that man's forehead?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Has anyone talked to you about your testimony here today in preparation for your testimony here today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: No one at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, no one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So, for instance, you did not talk to Mr. Turone about your testimony here today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. About your testimony here before this Tribunal have you talked to anyone about your testimony before the Tribunal here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Who all was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With Mr. Giuliano.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Was there anyone else that you discussed it with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Did anyone tell you that counts 1 and 2 of the indictment allege specifically that an SDA badge was nailed to that man's head?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you repeat this question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Sure. I am happy to. Did anyone tell you, after you made your statement in February 1996, that count -- where you said that it was an SDS badge that was nailed to Mr. Gotovac's head, that counts 1 and 2 of the indictment, specifically paragraph 16 of the indictment, say that the badge involved was an SDA badge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, nobody told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am about to mention something that I think we might want to go into private session for one question. If we just turn off the audio outside?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes. Can we get into private session. Tell them. (In closed session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We can return to open session (In open session)

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: When Mr. Gotovac was taken out and beaten, that incident that you recounted when you testified here last week, who else would have seen that? Who else could have seen that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For Mr. Scepo Gotovac?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could be seen by Mirko Babic and a group of men who were sitting there in those rows next to the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: They could see just as well as you could?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: You said that -- you testified that at some point Mr. Delic came to you and asked you about some injuries that you had received; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Did you get some medical care in any relationship to the time after that? For instance, after Mr. Delic talked to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken to Number 22, where there were doctors Relja and Petko, and there they changed the bandage that I had on my arm. They did not have any other supplies to do anything further.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So immediately after Mr. Delic talked to you you received what medical care was available?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: You also testified about one incident where you say that Mr. Delic beat you. Is that the incident you recounted in your statement, where he talked to you about not being allowed to walk around the Hangar 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you repeat this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Sure. I am happy to. You testified last week that Mr. Delic personally beat you on one occasion. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That was the incident that you talked about in your statement, where he said that prisoners were not supposed to be walking around -- moving around inside Hangar 6; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: In fact, that was the rule in Hangar 6, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And, in fact, you had violated that rule, had you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That is fine, sir. By the way, from your experience being around the Celebici camp, was that camp, in your opinion, a place that was designed to hold large numbers of prisoners, or was it designed to do something else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Well, for instance, from what you saw of the camp, were there facilities that you would expect to see if a large number of people were going to be kept there or stationed there, barracks and showers and toilet facilities and kitchens and recreational facilities and that kind of thing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that there was a room where there was the administration building. I know that there was a mess hall there, and there was also a toilet in there, but for the rest I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: But you never saw large numbers of facilities for things like toilets, or showers, or anything like that, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And, in fact, that place was designed -- the camp, when it was built, was designed to do things other than have large numbers of people living there; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: The food you received at Celebici, sir, do you know how it compared to the food that the guards were eating, whether you had greater rations or smaller rations than the guards had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what the guards were getting, but our food was horrible. We would have a slice of bread and later there was a period of three days and nights where we had no food.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point we will pass the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Any other cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Take the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness N. I am going to ask you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You are right. I want to ask you to give me the same courtesy that you gave Mr. Moran also and please attempt to listen to the question and give the answer to the question I am asking and then we will both be finished before lunch, I think. Can you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you. You stated earlier that the only person that you spoke to before you came to testify before this Tribunal was Mr. Giuliano Turone; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I talked in the period before with -- and I can't recall the names -- the gentleman asked me about that, but I know that here I only talked to Mr. Giuliano.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Let us go back to before you arrived in The Hague. You know you spoke to the investigators for the prosecution, did you not, in 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You also spoke to a Dusika Bojic, who is Secretary of the Association of Detainees, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So you never spoke to that person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have heard of this person, but I have not personally spoken to her.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Did you speak to a representative of hers before you came to testify at this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know who her representative is.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You discussed this case with someone from the Association of Detainees in Belgrade, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not this case.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Not your testimony, not the occurrence that happened in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not about the testimony, but we talked about what happened to me personally.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You talked to them about the testimony of other witnesses too, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You spoke to a man named Slobodan Stojanovic, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So you never spoke to the attorney for the Association of Detainees, did you? Is that what your testimony is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Is it your testimony before this court today that you have never been told what other witnesses have testified to or will testify to in this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You have never been informed about any testimony of anybody else before this Tribunal, only yours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not to me.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now you stated before that your occupation is still that of a refugee, but you have training as a machinist and training in the restaurant industry, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: It has been five years since your release from Celebici, has it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So who is it that pays for you to continue being a refugee?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that. I have no financial help. I work as a waiter and I sort of make ends meet.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You are no longer a refugee. You have a job now at this point, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not a steady job. I make ends meet, and, of course, I still am a refugee. I have nothing of my own.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: I want to go back to before the war started. You were a member -- you served in the ex-JNA, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: That ex-JNA was really the Serbian JNA in 1992, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Are you telling this court it was not predominantly Serbian in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That I don't know, but I know that there were Muslims and Croats in the JNA in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You served in the area of Mostar in the fight against the Croats for Dubrovnik and that area, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. That is not correct. In 1987/1988 I did my military duty in Tolmin in Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you. As a JNA soldier you are aware that ordinary soldiers are meant to follow orders, are they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Ordinary soldiers -- you were an ordinary soldier in the JNA, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: As an ordinary soldier, you have to follow the orders of your superior, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depends.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Are you saying that you did not follow the orders of your superior?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whatever I considered as something that I should do, I did that, but if there was something that for me personally was something I shouldn't do, I would not.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You would be punished if you did not follow orders, would you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depends. If I was right, I would not.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You said you are from the village of Viniste; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: In a little while after lunch I would like to show you a map to show where it is. It is in the middle of the area just north -- well, it is in the middle of the area between Bradina and Donje Selo, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depends on the position that you are looking from.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, if I might ask the usher to put this on the ELMO, I would like for him to demonstrate where his village is, so we can show why there was probably no armed conflict there. Thank you. This is an exhibit that has already been introduced in Ms Calic's testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Pointing).

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you. Viniste is a very small hamlet, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Can you just demonstrate one more time on this, right there on the map, you can see Viniste up in the mountains; right? Would you demonstrate one more time where it is located, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Pointing).

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you. Viniste -- is it not true that on May 19th 1992, that all of the military-aged men from Viniste had already gone to Donje Selo; is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: There were no fighting-aged men left in your village the day that the village was taken over, was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said already that there were military manoeuvres going past our village, and most of the people from that area were within the Homolje and Galjevo area, which was Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: In fact, most of the people had already left the village and gone to either Cerici or Donje Selo, had they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: There was no armed conflict in your village, was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You said that you were arrested in the -- arrested with Branko and Jordan Gotovac, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So if Branko Gotovac stated that he had not seen you until he got out of the van at Celebici, he would not be speaking the truth, would he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That I don't know, but Branko and myself and his son, Jordan, were all in the same vehicle, but it is possible that he did not notice it. Maybe he was afraid or something. He was in the vehicle with us.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So if Mr. Gotovac said that you were arrested with his son Jordan at Dervo Badzac's house in Homolje, that would not be the truth, would it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you repeat?

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So if Branko Gotovac said you were arrested with his son, Jordan, at Dervo Badzak's place, B-A-D-Z-A-K's place, in Homolje, he would not be speaking the truth; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The truth is that we were arrested in the house.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You were arrested in your home or in the home of Dervo Badzak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a mistake. Dervo -- it was the house of Hasib Jahic. They brought us there in order to protect us from this military that was passing through our hamlet and the day before, in fact, the same day, they were taken to Konjic and released by the HVO and the TO.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Then on your final arrest, you are stating to this court, that you were with Branko Gotovac and Jordan Gotovac at this gentleman's house just described. Was it in Homolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was in Galjevo. It is another hamlet just like Viniste, near Homolje, maybe 100 metres away. The distance between Galjevo and Homolje is 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your testimony is arrested with Branko and Jordan Gotovac, finally ultimately to go to Celebici at this location in this village you just described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jordan and myself were in the house. Branko was in Homolje in the house of Emir Alic. That same evening we were together taken to Celebici.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So you were not really arrested with them. You were arrested separately and then put together; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I said that Jordan and I were together in this house and this is the third time illustrating this, and Branko was in Emir Alic's house, but we were taken all together to Celebici. I hope I was clear.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. So it is clear that you were not with Branko Gotovac at the time that you were arrested, were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the moment I was in the van with Jordan and the van was in front of the house where Branko was staying. That is Emir Alic's house. Then he was put into the van there.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: The gentleman's house where you and Jordan Gotovac were located, he is a Muslim too, is he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: In fact, at one time you and Branko Gotovac and the Muslim soldiers, they were all drinking coffee at the home of Branko Gotovac, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That same day when we were returned from Konjic we first went to Branko Gotovac's house and on the suggestion of these people, who had taken us back from Konjic, we were in Branko Gotovac's house and then we moved to Homolje in order to get protection so that we would not be taken from Viniste again.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So your arrest on that day was Serbians, Muslims, friendly, no violence, and the atmosphere was controlled, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this village there was no armed conflict. The relationships were friendly until the day when we were taken to Celebici.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you. I suppose you did not know that Jordan Gotovac was arrested in the possession of a semi-automatic weapon, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That I am not familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: I want to go back a little bit. You were born in Bosnia-Herzegovina, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. You could have voted in the referendum on March 1st, 1992, could you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You could have voted in any election in Bosnia-Herzegovina, because you are a citizen of Bosnia-Herzegovina and you were of voting age, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I participated in elections I do not know exactly now, but in 1991. I did not participate in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You said you were not beaten when you were arrested, nor when you were first taken to Celebici; is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You said when you arrived at Celebici, you were placed in Building Number 22, with some other detainees, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You also stated that several nights later you heard some -- you saw some people from Bradina being brought in, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in the day-time. In the day-time, yes, I saw them bringing in some people.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You also testified that you knew these people from Bradina, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: But you also stated that you did not know that they were even from Bradina until later on when you got into Building Number 6; is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Not that I did not know. I assumed they were from Bradina, but later I saw some of them.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Also you state that in Building Number 22, when you were first placed in there, there were about 30-40 other detainees in the building with you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So there were not over 100 detainees in that building during that time, were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time I arrived there were roughly that many that I said, and I know that at one time, while I was in that building, there were about 100 people.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So are you saying that the population in Building Number 22 increased after you arrived, or after you went to Hangar Number 6? Which one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While I was in the Building Number 22 the number of people increased.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You and Mr. Branko Gotovac were neighbours and friends, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You knew about his hernia before you were taken to Celebici, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You have discussed your experiences in Celebici with him since 1992, have you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember talking to him in particular, but I know what happened to Branko in Celebici.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Are you telling us that since 1992 in casual conversation you and Mr. Gotovac have not told each other what happened to each other in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not have any reason to talk about those things, because we saw what had happened to him and me.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now you described three serious beatings that you allege you received while at Celebici, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I described all the torture I was subjected to. Some of them I failed to mention, this beating where they hit me. I mentioned the worst ones.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: That is what my question was. You described three very serious beatings, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I described the beating up and the burning with a heated knife.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: The first beating that you described, I believe you said took place on May 24th, 1992, did it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: On that day you were beaten by the HOS soldiers, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Well, the soldiers that you were beaten by were not merely the people present in Celebici camp, were they? They were MUP representatives and Croatian soldiers too, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I just know that I was beaten by Bato Alikadic and Almir Nuhic, and the only Croat there was Pero Blazevic, known as Srbija, as far as I knew.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you. In fact, Esad Landzo was nowhere around Celebici during this period of the time, was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: But you did not -- he was not beating you that day, was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that day, no.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And, in fact, you never saw Esad Landzo present in the camp until he came with some other guards around the middle of June, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the date exactly when he came.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: But it was after -- I am sorry -- but it was after you were taken to Hangar Number 6, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You said you received broken ribs, severe beating in the kidney area, a cracked jaw, two teeth knocked out and several teeth cracked, all from the beating on May 24th, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on May 24th two teeth were broken and my jaw was fractured. After that I was beaten up several times and I described those incidents in my statement, one of those beatings.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: In the beating on May 24th, that is when you were beaten so severely that you lost control of your kidneys; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The second time when I was beaten up I had no control over my kidneys.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Well, you said on May 24th that in your testimony last week that after the beating on May 24th your friends had had to carry you to the toilet and you could not eat or drink. In fact, they dropped some milk and some liver on your lips; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You said you remained in Building Number 22 for 13 days and then you were transferred to Hangar Number 6. So that would be somewhere after June 5th, would it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
