utterances.text: Roughly 13 days. I did not say exactly 13 days, and I was transferred. I don't know the date. I was moved to Hangar Number 6.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: I would like to ask you some questions about Hangar Number 6 right now. You spent most of your time there, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And that is -- what would you estimate the dimensions of that building were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, roughly it was about 25 metres long and about 13, 14 wide. I didn't have a meter to measure it, so I don't know exactly. That is my rough estimate. Considering the condition I was in, I need not necessarily know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: There were windows at the top of this building, if you can call them windows, really more like air vents, that were at least 3 metres above the ground, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how high up they were but they were in the corner, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: But you could not see out of them, could you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those windows were facing behind the part of the -- the area where people were beaten. People were taken out of the hangar and beaten and there were no windows there.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: The windows that you are describing, though, they were too high for any human being to be able to see out of without a ladder; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody needed to look through those windows, because one could not see anything through them anyway. There were just some hangars further away.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Were they too high to see out of or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really don't know exactly. I never looked through them.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now, the front of the hangar, or the walls of the hangar, all four walls, there were no holes in the walls that you could see out of, were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't pay any attention, so I don't know whether there were holes or not, any kinds of holes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And there was no electricity in Hangar Number 6, was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know, but the lights were never switched on for us.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So at day-time you had the natural light from the high windows, but at night-time there was no electricity, no light bulbs, no lights with which to see; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't notice. I'm speaking in my personal name.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Was there a light in the building at night or no light in the building at night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't notice any light.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now you talked about the food being absolutely horrible, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And the food came from outside of the camp, did it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know where it came from.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You knew that the food was not prepared in the camp, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You knew a young man named Sok, an Albanian, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And he stayed at the Celebici camp after the JNA left, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how he came to stay. I just know I would see him there when I was brought there.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And he was in charge of distributing the food in Celebici, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Well, you knew that there were two prisoners from your Hangar Number 6 that would come to the Albanian and get the food and take it back to the hangar; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know who went for the food, but I don't know where they went.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: The names of the two prisoners who went for the food are what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am asking you to please tell us the names of the prisoners who went for the food, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ratko Cecez and Mladen Mrkajic went often.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: In fact, they were the representatives of the prisoners in Hangar Number 6 that would communicate with the guards, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were representatives of the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Mr. Esad Landzo never distributed any food, did he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And he was just a prison guard, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that Esad Landzo was -- that he beat and tortured prisoners. I don't know what he was.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Do you remember our promise earlier that you would answer my question. Esad Landzo was merely a prison guard, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was just a prison guard.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now, the people in charge of providing food for the detainees and water for the detainees and medical attention for the detainees, that would not be a prison guard, would it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know who was responsible for that.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You stated earlier that -- you drew a map and you showed where you were sitting in the hangar in the summer of 1992, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You changed positions some time around 1st July, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date when I moved.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: I think it was some time during the middle of your stay at Celebici that you changed positions; is that not what you testified to last week?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said roughly that it was then, but I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now, you know that the prisoners were not allowed to walk around Hangar Number 6 without permission, were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a prohibition on movement in the hangar. You weren't allowed to get up from your place either.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now, there was a time when you were allowed to wave and communicate with your mother while you were in Hangar 6, was there not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On one occasion this was allowed, but I don't know who of the guards was there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You would not have been able to communicate with your mother if you had not received permission to go to the door and wave to her; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: In fact, you know that Esad Landzo was the one who gave you permission to stand at the door for two or three minutes and wave to your mother; is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not Esad Landzo.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So are you telling this court under oath that Esad Landzo -- that you did not tell Esad Landzo: "Thank you, Zenga, for letting me see my mother. I won't forget that ever." That is the truth, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not for that. I do not remember saying that to him.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Any guard who would have let you go to the door and let you communicate to your mother, probably would have been punished for that, would he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not manage to talk. We could just raise our hand and I don't know what the consequences for the guard could be.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now, last Monday, when you were giving testimony, you were smiling at Mr. Landzo, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but because after all I survived, after all the things he did to me. That's why I smiled.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now, the second beating that you described you allege happened on July 15th, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't say that the second beating happened on July 15th. On July 15th I was taken out and burnt with a heated knife on my legs and arms.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Well, I believe your testimony last Monday was that you were taken out of the hangar and a gasmask was put on your face. Is that not how it started?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Then you stated that the screw on the front of the gasmask was tightened so you could not breathe. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Then you testified that there was a fire outside, that a knife could be heated in; is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. A piece of cloth was set fire to, first some paper and then this cloth, some kind of a bag or something -- I don't remember was the material was. It was in this fire that the knife was heated.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So this was not a big bonfire or anything. This was a linen bag that had been set on fire; is that what your testimony is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a linen bag was burning and in this fire the knife was heated.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So how long was this period of the alleged torture that you described outside of Hangar 6? Five minutes, ten minutes, fifteen minutes, 30 minutes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Roughly about 30 minutes. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. You claim that Mr. Landzo heated this knife in this fire of the burning bag and then he burned your right hand; is that not what you stated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First my left, then my right, then both my legs.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Then you stated he heated the knife began in the fire and then you stated he burned your left thigh; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was my left hand, then he heated the knife again, then my right hand, then the knife was heated again, and then my left leg was burned below the knee, and then two more burns on my left thigh and my right.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Well, you are not telling this court there were sterno inside that linen bag, are you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what was there.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So you have just described four times of heating a burning knife all from the flame of a burning linen bag; is that your testimony, over a 30 minute period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how many times he heated the knife, but I know the first time he made three burns on my left hand from this one heating. On my right hand he made three or four burns. Again if you don't believe me, you can look. You have the evidence. You have the pictures.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Well, I would like to look, but we talked about the thighs before and I am going to spare both of us that embarrassment right now. We are going to rely on photographs later. Thank you, though. All of this time, the 30 minutes that you have been heating the knife, burning, heating the knife, burning, heating the knife, burning, you have a gasmask on and you cannot breathe; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Occasionally he would take the stopper out so that I could get some air, and when he made those burns, then he would put the plug back in so that I couldn't scream and I was, of course, choking, but I'm saying again I didn't say that it was exactly 30 minutes. I said roughly 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Then you testified that the mask was removed and you asserted that he hit you with a chain, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now, the truth is there was not any chain around at Celebici, was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know, but a piece of chain about maybe 20 cms long, which he took out on that occasion and started hitting me with it on the neck. That I saw with my own eyes and felt on my own skin.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: The truth is that the chain -- you were hit with a chain, but it was on May 24th, and it was by Mr. Alikadic and Nuhic, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. On 24th I wasn't beaten with a chain. I was beaten with a stick and a cable or whatever, but on this day, when Esad Landzo burnt me, he hit me with a chain on the neck.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now when you were in Hangar Number 6 -- and you walked back to Hangar Number 6, did you not, after this incident on July 15th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on 15th.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: In fact, when you walked in, you stated last Monday that your friend said: "Gosh! You escaped without any problems, did you not, because we didn't hear you scream?" Is that not what you stated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So your friends must not have thought you were in very much pain, did they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They couldn't conclude that I had no pains, but it was customary when people were taken out and beaten and tortured we would hear the screams, but as I had a mask over my head, they couldn't hear my voice. However, when I showed them all those burns they were flabbergasted, and the worst of it is that I was the first victim. Afterwards others were victimised. There was petrol poured over them and lit and in other ways --

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Excuse me. You knew another gentleman in Hangar Number 6 named Miljanic, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Miljanic?

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Gojko Miljanic was there, his son Savo, Nedjo Miljanic, Slovko Miljanic.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: In fact, the older men like Mr. Gojko Miljanic, or whichever is the older Miljanic, they would save their bread to eat at night, would they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: In fact, you got in a fight with Mr. Miljanic, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With Miljanic? Which Miljanic?

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: The older gentleman Miljanic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And his first name?

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: I guess it is Gojko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think Gojko was dead by then. He died in his son's arms.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Well, one Mr. Miljanic you got in a fight with because -- it is Nedeljko Miljanic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So you never got in a fight with Mr. Nedeljko Miljanic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So if he stated that you -- well, if he had gone to the guards and reported that you had been stealing the bread from the old men, he would be lying then; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not true, that I stole bread, because I couldn't get up from my position, nor did any of the prisoners steal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think we can have a break for lunch at this point. When we come back, you can continue with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly invite the witness. He is still on his oath. (Witness re-entered court)

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you that you are still testifying under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: You can continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. I believe that we were about to talk about the third beating that you described, but before I go into that one, I would like to ask you: during this time you were beaten by the HOS or MUP soldiers, when they put Serbian money in your mouth and beat you, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honours, I would like to bring out -- because I asked earlier about putting these on the video thing, but Blaskic has the computer all tied up, so I would like to bring out Prosecution Exhibit number 1 and ask that -- I think the Registrar will have to get it out -- ask that drawing Number 7 be placed on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You mean photograph Number 7?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Number 7 is the drawing of the inside, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Quite right. It is Hangar Number 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. It is the inside of Hangar Number 6. Witness N, you described two different locations, one where you sat at the first of your stay at Celebici, and one location where you stayed the second part of your stay at Celebici. Can you, without making any marks on, this because this is direct evidence, can you point with your finger where inside the hangar was your first location and then the second place that you sat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I showed that last time. I thought it was not necessary, but of course, I can do it. Roughly here the first time and later here. (Pointing).

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: The place where you sat the second time, which is further back in the hangar, that is where you were sitting when Mr. Esad Landzo first came to the camp, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. The second place that you were sitting, that is where you were sitting at the time that Scepo Gotovac was allegedly beaten; is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly whether I was there, but I do think that it was in the first position that I was sitting at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Can you show the court on this drawing, on this diagram, where it was exactly that Mirko Babic was sitting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can. (Pointing).

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: The truth is he was not in the second row?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Roughly here.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: He was in the third row back, was he not, not the first row in the centre but the second row in the centre; is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mirko Babic was sitting in the second row in the middle at first, roughly here. I can't tell you exactly. He was facing this part of the hangar with his back. His back was turned. (Pointing).

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Just for clarification, the first row was the group of detainees against the wall. The second row was the row closer to the door in the centre, and the third row was the row in the centre that is furthest from the door. That is where Mirko Babic was sitting, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was not far from the door, because the difference between this row and the other one was about a metre, one and a half, so it wasn't far.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So your testimony to this court was the two rows in the centre were just one metre away from each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am giving approximations. One metre, one and a half. I don't know exactly. I didn't say it was one metre.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Could I please have the usher put Prosecution Photograph number 27 onto the ELMO? No, that is not number 27 according to my book. Yes. I cannot tell. No, that is not the same photograph either that I have. Oh, your Honour, I believe that the numbers we have are different.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now, Witness N, can you look at this photograph and do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first or the second? The first or the second photograph?

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: The top one, the one at the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: That is the front of Hangar Number 6, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: With your little pointer right there can you point on this photograph where it is that the one opening that was used in Hangar Number 6 was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean "opening"? You mean the door?

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, I mean the door.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Pointing).

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: That is not a large hangar door, is it? It is a smaller door, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your testimony is that you could see out of this door and see what was happening out of Hangar Number 6 when you were in position number 1 in the hangar; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I could see in front of the door when they were open.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now, the door opens not from the corner of the hangar but it opens from the middle part of the hangar, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: The door does not swing open --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: You can be running away with too many imaginations here. This was a fairly difficult thing. You cannot even know what the place looks like. He has told you he could see from where he was sitting. It depends on the way the door was opened. If it was open, he might have seen it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might, the way the door opened obscures the way he would be able to see. If it opens out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: You did not open it, did you?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: No, but I know how it opens. I have a right to test his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: You have too many rights. This is not one of them. He has told you when the door was open, he was able to see. You did not open the door for him to see, so you do not know how much you opened it for him to see.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am just trying to prove that if the door were wide open that his line of vision is, one, obscured by this hill here and, number two, that the door opens in a way to limit his view, where all he has is the side of the hill that he sees at that point. If the court wants to cut me off from my questioning, fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: If it is being unreasonable, I shall tell you. If you want to push it, ask him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Does the door open from the corner of the hangar out or does it open from the middle of the hangar out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you I don't know exactly which way it opens. I didn't open it myself.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: But the truth is when you looked out of that hangar, all you could see was the side of that hill, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We were not looking through the hangar, but through the open door, so I could see in that direction what there was in front of the door.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour, could I please have Prosecution photograph number 33?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: You can have the exhibits -- you can use as many of them as you want to. It is an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I was just asking for him to place it onto the ELMO for me, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Witness N, those windows are the only windows on the front of this hangar, are they not. I am referring to Prosecution witness (sic) number 33 and Hangar Number 6.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: The windows that you see here on the front of Hangar Number 6 are the only windows on the front of Hangar Number 6, are they not? I am referring to photograph number 33, the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Those windows are --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Those windows are definitely too high for anybody to look out of without a window (sic), are they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I personally did not look. I didn't even notice those windows.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Let us go on to the third beating that you described. That beating that you described was the day that you said 22 people were taken out and beaten, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It was the evening.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: That happened on July 17th, did it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't give the date.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Well, you were given a reason why everybody was taken out and beaten, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: In fact, this was the day that the nine military police were murdered near Bradina, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And you are positive that was not the same day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It wasn't that day.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You stated you were taken behind Hangar Number 6 and another gasmask was placed over your head, did you not, only this time it had a white cloth placed over the front of it so you could not see; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was taken out of the hangar, round the corner, where the path led to the toilet, and that is where they beat me from the front side of the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: When you say around the side, you can point on this photograph where it was you were taken. You were taken to the back left-hand side or right-hand side of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You testified there were four or five people that held you down and beat you; is that not true, with something resembling a baseball bat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now you were --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a wooden object in the shape of a baseball bat, and before that we were beaten with a baseball bat too.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now, you were not stripped naked at that time, were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They took off everything I had on me. They forced me on my stomach and they beat me and they poured water over me.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: The truth is that whatever happened back there, you do not know who beat you. It just happened that the only voice you recognised was Esad Landzo's; is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Esad Landzo personally took me out of the hangar. He put the mask on my head and Esad Landzo hit me several times with his leg in the stomach and the ribs until I fell, and Esad Landzo held me down until this unknown -- while this unknown person was beating me.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. So now your story is that Esad Landzo held you down while some unknown person beat you. Is that what you are testimony is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I said, that Esad Landzo took me out of the hangar, that there were another four or five people there, that they held me and one of them was beating me. So Esad Landzo was holding me down and two or three other people, other persons. One was standing on my legs and the other two on my hands.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: The truth is that once the gasmask was put on your face and you had the white cloth over it, you do not know who was beating you or who was holding you, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that Esad Landzo was holding me, because when they were beating me, he would speak some words that I did not understand, but I recognised his voice.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Let me ask you another question too. You have testified many times about how you know that Mr. Landzo beat people, because he took them out of the hangar. The truth is that you assumed that Mr. Landzo was beating people because he was the one who was ordered to take the detainees out of the hangar; is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was given such orders, but Landzo came to the hangar often. He beat me in front of all the prisoners. Afterwards he took me out and beat me, but I don't know who gave him any orders and whether those were orders that he was following.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: But this testimony that you just gave is certainly different from your direct testimony a week ago Monday, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Listen, after all, five years have gone by and what was done to me during my stay in Celebici, it's a wonder that I can talk at all and especially when I remember all those things that I went through. This is the clear evidence that can be confirmed by 200 people.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You testified earlier that you did not know whether Esad Landzo was a guard at Celebici or not. Was that not your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I said that I didn't know whether he was a guard or not. I just know that he beat people, that he came, that he was there during that period non-stop. We were all afraid.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now, Witness N, we had an agreement earlier that you would answer my question. My question was: you said earlier that you did not know whether Esad Landzo was a prison guard or not. Did you or did you not say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I am repeating again what I already said. I do not know whether he was a guard, but I know that he was there. He beat people. He tortured people. I think that is clear. I have nothing more to say.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now, Witness N, Mr. Landzo in 1992 was only 18 or 19 years old, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how old he was.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: But you knew he was very young, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And in reality you don't know one way or the other whether he was just following orders, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You stated you were outside with Branko and Danilo Gotovac whenever Branko Gotovac was beaten. Is that what your testimony was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I was with Branko Gotovac when Zenga beat him, and on that occasion he stuck a match under my thumbnail, after which I had a lot of trouble. It became painful. It was very painful and it hasn't healed properly to this day.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So your testimony is that Branko Gotovac was outside with you when this occurred. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Branko was there and Danilo, his son, was there when this happened to me.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So it is a little strange that Mr. Gotovac never mentioned that incident, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: What is the objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: He cannot be questioned about what other people said.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: It is just his personal opinion about whether it would be unusual that the other witness did not mention it, if he was supposed to be present whenever this occurred. I will change the question. When do you allege that the incident involving fellatio occurred? . Please do not mention any names, Witness N.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: When is it that you allege that the incident involving the fellatio occurred and please do not mention any names, just a date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the date exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: But you do know that you were sitting in your second position in the hangar when that occurred, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't say for sure where I was sitting, but I know I saw it and it's not important where I was sitting, but I saw it and it was not just me who saw it; all the prisoners who were there saw it.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Last Monday on page 1913 of the court record you stated that you personally viewed Mirko Babic, Vukasin Mrkajic and Dusko Bendzo and one other person with their pants still burning in the hangar. Did you not testify to that on page 1913 of the court record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stated regarding Dusko Bendzo, I saw his pants burning. As for Vukasin Mrkajic, I saw him when a fuse was wound round him and a light was put to it and he was running round. Regarding Mirko Babic, I saw burns.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am sorry. That is not my question. My question is: you saw their pants still on fire in the hangar. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have just said I saw Dusko Bendzo's pants burning, and in the case of Vukasin, he was naked to the waist and this fuse was wound round his body and it was burning. Mirko Babic, I saw the burn, the scar on his leg. I didn't say that his pants were burning. Only Dusko Bendzo's pants were burning inside. That is what I saw and said.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now, you testified on Monday that Scepo Gotovac was taken out of the hangar by Esad Landzo, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: The truth is that all you know is that Mr. Landzo took him out of the hangar; is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that he was beaten by Esad Landzo there and in front of the hangar and that he had taken him out. That's what I know, and I also know that there was this badge that had been nailed to his head, to his forehead.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Witness N, the truth is that once Mr. Gotovac was taken out of the hangar by Mr. Landzo, you did not personally witness what happened to him outside, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see it personally, what happened outside, but we heard the moans, cries for help of Scepo Gotovac and then later there was somebody who had seen Esad Landzo beat him. I don't want to --

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am going to object. He is not testifying from any personal knowledge. He is citing that somebody else may have told him something later on. I asked him if he saw it and he needs to answer that question. Could the court instruct him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Instruct him to do what, to answer your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: The truth is once he is outside, you do not know what happened. You could not personally have seen that, could you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I had seen when he was beaten inside. That is what I saw with my own eyes and I saw that he took him out and we heard the screams outside. That meant that he was being beaten and then later the people were saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Are you satisfied with this?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I have two questions for the witness. How wide was this door out of which a prisoner was taken out? How wide was it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I thought he had given answers to that. He need not answer that. He has given answers how he saw people were taken out. He has answered that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How wide was the door?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: You do not have to answer that, because he is not making any claims for seeing people from inside. He did say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The second question is: was the door allowed to remain open after the prisoner was taken out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depended. Sometimes the door would remain open and sometimes they would shut it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you. The truth is, Witness N, that you do not know whether Mr. Landzo was merely following orders either, do you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: This is your third time of asking this question and you do not have to continue with it that way. This is your third question on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am asking specifically about Scepo Gotovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: He had always told you he could not know. This is your third time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: You testified on Monday that an SDS badge had been nailed into his forehead, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. On Monday I stated that a badge had been nailed. I don't know whether it was an SDS or SDA badge, but I just know that there was a badge nailed to his head through his skin.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And the truth is you don't know who placed the badge on Mr. Gotovac before he was brought back into the hangar, so you could not personally know who placed it there, could you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Did you know who placed the badge in his forehead?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard from other people that it was Esad Landzo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: No. Did you know who did it? Did you see them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see it personally. I did not see the instance when the badge was nailed but some people said that it was Esad Landzo, because he had beaten him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: In fact, Witness N --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's what I heard. I said that I had heard. I saw the badge that was nailed there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: That was not the question. This all happened at night, did it not, this whole incident with Scepo Gotovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It happened during the day.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So if Mirko Babic testified that Adem Cosic and someone else other than Esad Landzo took Scepo Gotovac out of the hangar, then he would be lying, would he not -- I am sorry -- telling an untruth? I am sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that Esad Landzo took Gotovac out of the hangar and I know that it was during the day. I don't know what Mirko Babic stated and that's of no interest to me. I know what I know and I didn't know those persons.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: It is your testimony today that this all happened during broad daylight, not at night; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Objection. Asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, during the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He said broad daylight.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Did you not testify last Monday that you merely found Mr. Gotovac dead the next morning? Is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not say about Mr. Gotovac that he was found dead in the morning, that he had died there.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You did not say that he was brought back in in the middle of the night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No. I did not say that he had been taken in during the night. I said that he was brought back and that he died there. I did not say that it was in the morning or during the night, as you say.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. You testified that with Simo Jovanovic, he was taken outside of the hangar too; is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He was taken out of the hangar, beaten outside -- he was first beaten inside and then he was --

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am going to object. He was testifying from no personal knowledge outside. If he was beaten inside, yes. He is not answering the questions. This is going to take all day. Could I just ask for an instruction from the court to have him answer the questions, please? .

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Keep asking him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Simo Jovanovic was taken outside of the hangar, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was taken out and he was brought back, and he was also beaten inside, so I saw when he was beaten inside and I could hear when he was being beaten outside.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So then your testimony last Monday --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him dead.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Last Monday when you testified that you did not even know who took him out of the hangar, then that is not true, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Objection. This is amounting to a harrassment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: What is your answer to the question? Ask him the question again.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: So when you testified last Monday that you did not even know who took him out of the hangar, Simo Jovanovic, that would not be telling the truth, would it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that there was a group of people who were from the village of Idbar and Esad Landzo was with them. That is what I said. I didn't say that I didn't know who took him out. Maybe the interpretation was not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So your testimony today is that there was a group of people that took him out; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a group of people standing at the door when they called him out to get out of the hangar, and Esad Landzo even beat him inside in front of everybody before he went out. Then later he was beaten and we saw the dead body behind our backs there.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So all this is completely different from your testimony a week ago last Monday, is it not, though?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not different at all. Maybe just a word or two that are different. What is important is that I saw his dead body and I saw him being taken out, and I saw when he was beaten inside.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And all of this happened at night, did it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it didn't happen at night. It happened in the early evening, but it was still daylight.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So was it before 9 o'clock or after 9 o'clock?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the exact time. We did not have any watches.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Now whenever you testified about the beating of Bosko Samoukovic, you never mentioned that there were a lot of other guards present at the time, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know who it was. I saw personally when Bosko Samoukovic was beaten and I saw Esad Landzo beat him with a plank across his back and then he was taken out and I said that Dr Relja told us that he had died in Building Number 22 and he had been brought there.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: This was July 17th, 1992, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what date it was. I don't know the date.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now, you left Celebici at the end of August; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 31st August.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You told the Prosecutor that while you were in Musala that you saw Mr. Landzo occasionally, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And he was a member of the military police then, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now, you never saw Mr. Landzo in Celebici before the middle of June and the HOS soldiers left, did you -- I mean, the HVO. I am sorry. It was the HVO soldiers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is not clear to me. I do not know when the HVO members were there. I just know that at the beginning they were together. While I was in Building Number 22 I know that there were Croats there. After that I don't know. I did not notice Croatian soldiers when I was in Building Number 6.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You were aware that there was a group of prison guards that came together, like six or seven of them at one time to Celebici; is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know the exact dates. I don't know when these groups came and when it was that somebody arrived, because there were many guards.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now, you left at the end of August. You never saw Esad Landzo in the prison camp after the end of July, did you, 1st August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: I pass the witness, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mrs. Residovic, I pass the witness to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you, your Honour. Good afternoon, Witness N?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Edina Residovic. I am the defence counsel for Zejnil Delalic. Mr. N, I will ask a few questions on his behalf. I will also ask you, just as my colleagues did, to answer my questions as briefly as possible, and if you cannot understand my question, please tell me that immediately and I will try and rephrase the question in such a way that would be the easiest for you to answer; is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness N, before I start asking you questions about the events that you are familiar with and that you testified to before this court, I would like to ask you to help me identify certain persons. I would like to have these photographs marked for identification purposes and to be shown to Witness N for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Sorry. We are not familiar with these photos, so we would like to know what the defence lawyer is going to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: They will be passed to you. They will be passed to you first. Show it to the prosecution: let the prosecution see them. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honour, yes. We would ask the photographs to be placed on the ELMO so that everybody can see them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Let them know what actually they are. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Yes. Of course, yes, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: We are very sorry, your Honours, but this is a matter of general concern. We were not absolutely informed about this possibility of showing pictures to the witness and these seem not to be pictures intending to impeachment but seem to be part of the defence case maybe. I do not know. So we object to the proper way of introducing evidence this way. I am very sorry. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, I very clearly stated the request of the defence. For the purpose of identification of certain persons I wish that the witness be shown the statements or photographs and then during the cross-examinations they can also be used to verify whether the witness speaks truth about certain facts, and that is the reason why I want these pictures, as is my right, to be shown to the witness, and whether they will be used as evidence or not, the defence will decide on that after the cross-examination and possible identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually I do not really know what it is all about, but you do not spring a surprise on somebody by merely showing him a picture unless he has denied knowing who the person is in that picture. If you actually want him to identify a person, there has to be a background as to his knowledge of that person. There is nothing now before the Trial Chamber to show that he has ever denied knowing whoever you want to show to him to identify it. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): It is clear that once the picture is shown to him, that I will ask him questions about these persons. This is an integral part of the identification process. If the witness does not have a picture in front of him, I cannot ask him the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Are you trying to remind him about the persons in the photograph or are you actually leading him into telling you exactly what has transpired between him and someone and this picture tells you who that person is? You must lay the background of how this picture comes into it. It is not fair on anybody just to spring a surprise on him. I am sure you know why you want to show him the photographs. You know in your mind why you want him to see the photographs. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Naturally, your Honour, during my cross-examination my intention is, depending on whether the witness will or not identify the person, I intend to ask him some questions. That is the reason why I offer these photographs. They have a bearing on his testimony before this court. I can't tell you more at this point, because I would then reveal what questions I intend to ask of the witness and that witness had already --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: If he says he does not know, I do not know what you will do. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): I will continue with other questions. I do not expect the witness -- that the witness will have to answer or recognise the persons, but I think that -- since the witness is under oath, I think that the witness will tell us what he knows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Okay. Show it to him. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I would add for the record that our objection is based on Rule 67(c).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It is a special defence taken by the accused. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Please, I would like this photograph to be placed on the ELMO. Mr. N, do you know who this person is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You can put the next picture. Witness N, can you recognise the persons in this picture, any of the persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please show the third picture to the witness. This is the picture of a man with long hair and a ponytail?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recognise this man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw this man when he entered Hangar Number 6. I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I can help you, can you remember if this is Emir Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know his name. I just saw his face when he entered the camp. That's the only thing I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you saw this man enter Hangar Number 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please take the picture off the ELMO and we will go back to it later. Can you please now show to the witness the last photograph that we would like him to see? Mr. N, can you recognise the person in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw this person but I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where did you see this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember now exactly. This is not -- it seems to have been retouched, this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. N, did you see this person also in the Celebici barracks, in the Celebici camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is possible that I saw him there, but I am not sure. I did see him somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I may help you to remind you, because so much time has passed, is it true that this is Sefik Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you, Witness N, if you can, in your own hand on pictures number 3 and 4, to state before this court that you recognised the person who entered Hangar Number 6, that is picture number 3, and on photograph 4, if --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As for picture number 4, I am not sure. That's what I said. As for picture number 3, I am sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As for picture number 4, we will not write down those things. As for picture number 3, if you can write down what you said before this Court. Do you have a pen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: What is the meaning of that? What is the meaning of a witness writing down the record of the court? It is a record here. If there is anything he admitted, it is there. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): After this, your Honours, I wish photograph number 3 to be submitted as evidence for the defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: You mean through the prosecution witnesses? MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Yes, as evidence identified by the witness in this Trial Chamber, and afterwards it can be used as defence evidence by the court. Maybe I was not precise enough. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: It could be tendered as what he has identified. That is sufficient. It is an exhibit. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Yes. Thank you, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I object to the admission of this exhibit for a matter of principle, because we object under Rule 67(c), because we have never been given access to these pictures and it was not for impeachment reasons. So this is our objection, and I emphasise we object as a matter of principle. Defence know that we are entitled to see what should be used as evidence under Rule 67, paragraph C. Thank you. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, the defence will do that. Since the witness has identified only one photograph, from that moment we are obliged to discover evidence, because we intend to use this exhibit as evidence. According to the cited Rule, we are obliged to submit any evidence which we have in our possession and submit for insight to the Prosecutor and that is what we shall do now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: This is evidence which should have been submitted to them before now. The only relevance I see here is merely for identification purposes. It is merely identifying the particular photograph. I do not see the basis on which it has now been admitted into evidence, because there is nothing to follow that. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, the defence will tender this identified picture when presenting its case as evidence. At this moment it realises that it is its obligation to submit it to the Prosecutor in accordance with the Rule on reciprocal disclosure. I thank you now. The witness has identified the photograph. I would like to ask him to note this identification on the photograph so that when the defence uses it as evidence, it can be used as part of all the evidence before this Trial Chamber, and, of course, it will immediately be submitted to the prosecution in accordance with Rule 67(c).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber notes it is for identification. It is only in for identification purposes. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you, but I would like to ask the witness to note on picture 3, to put down with his hand that today he recognised on this picture --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I said you cannot do that. You cannot do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Why do you insist on that? It is already on the transcript that he has identified this man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, it is there. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you. I am not insisting. I know it is in the transcript, but since I have already noted that I am trying to discover how other people behaved before this Trial Chamber, the Prosecutor did the same, so I thought that was the correct procedure. For me it is sufficient that it is stated in the transcript that the witness has identified photograph number 3, but I think I was not acting improperly if I asked him to write that down in his own hand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Except it is not in his handwriting or you fear he is not the one giving the evidence ... The whole process is a very strange way, in a strange Trial Chamber, I suppose, but definitely he has answered. He has identified it and it has been admitted for identification purposes. This is sufficient. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): I will for the sake of precision regarding this identification and what is -- what appears in the transcript, let me repeat that the witness has identified the photograph submitted to him as number 3, and in answer to my question whether this was a man with long hair and a ponytail, and I named him as Emir Delalic. I want to be sure we do not make any mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: The witness did not give that evidence. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: His evidence is very clear in the transcript as to the person he saw in the Hangar 6. That is all he knew about it. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you, your Honours. Mr. N, I should now like to pass on to some questions that I am interested in hearing from you. You told the Prosecutor in February 1996 a lengthy statement; you made a lengthy statement for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You made it in Temisoara?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Like my learned colleague, in view of the next three questions I intend to ask the witness, I ask that the sound be switched off so as not to affect the protective measures against this witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly inform them to cut off the sound so it should be in private session. (In private session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: (redactedû (redactedû

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: (In open session) MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Mr. N, the statement of February last year, which you gave to the prosecution, you gave it over two days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, about. I was there for two days. I can't remember exactly the hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That statement was quite an exhaustive one and with a great deal of detail and precision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what you think about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I am asking you to answer my question rather than answering with your questions. Will you please, your Honours, ask the witness to answer my questions, but not with counter-questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: What was your question, because there has been a dialogue between the two of you? MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Please, can you tell me whether at the time you conveyed everything you knew and that you could remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time you said and mentioned people and events that were linked to your arrest and your detention in Celebici and Musala; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That was February 1996; true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly the date. Yes, I know it was 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time the proceedings before this court had not yet started; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But at the time you, Mr. N, were not aware who might be indicted by this Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were born in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You knew many people in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you could not know which of those people would be indicted by the International Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, Mr. N, that at the time you told the Prosecutor that all that you said in your statement was true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was the truth that I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were aware at the time, and you were warned of this, that this statement may be used in proceedings before this Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand. I made a statement probably for this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. N, I just wish to go back to some of your indications in connection with our questions. On several occasions you testified that you wished to forget many events, that you do not like to remember what is behind you, and I fully appreciate that, because all of us that have experienced the war wish to suppress many of those memories. However, I would, after all, like to ask you to tell me or to confirm that a year ago you probably remembered some events better, some events and people, than you can today, or maybe you will be able to in a year's time; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After that statement in February last year you had no need to look for the Prosecutor or the Association of Detainees in connection with that statement. Did you have any such need?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the Prosecution or the Association of Detainees look for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that, after Temisoara?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You told my learned colleague, Mr. Moran, that upon your arrival in The Hague you spoke to the distinguished representative of the prosecution, Mr. Turone; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when I came here. I thought you were asking for events over there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, after that statement in Temisoara and before this interview in The Hague, did you make any additional statements?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean? To whom?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I met the Prosecution here only when I came here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you please tell me whether anyone informed you that the defence of Mr. Delalic or my learned colleagues, the defence counsel of the other accused, wished to talk to you so as to have the same chance as the prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, nobody told me that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer too. So let me repeat: after Temisoara you had no talks with the prosecution until you came to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I met the prosecutors here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. N, were you aware of the position of the Association that witnesses should beware of defence counsel and should not talk to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really do not know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. N, have you ever met with the investigator who questioned you in Temisoara, Mr. Sergio Saxaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And have you met a Mrs Sabine Manke of Germany?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but not linked to this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you are confirming that with Sabine Manke, that you did not make any statements?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What about Mrs Teresa McHenry? You did not meet her either before coming to The Hague; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you did not make any statement for Mrs. McHenry either?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now, Mr. N, like to ask you to look at the statement of November 14th. No. First let me ask you: you were born on 3rd December 1968, is that true, and the name of your father is Risto?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be supplied with a copy of his statement from November 1996, in which it says that the statement was made before the interviewer Sabine Manke and present during the interview was Mrs. Teresa McHenry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Do you recognise that as your statement? MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Mr. N, if it is easier for you, I can give you the first statement too, which is a lengthy one, and you were interviewed by Sergio Oaxaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Listen, this is all okay, but a moment ago when you asked me about Sabine, whether I had had any talks with her, you were talking about Temisoara. You didn't ask me about these interviews.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you give me this document? So in this document you recognise the statement you made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but there must be a mistake in the translation, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This was a statement made in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before Sabine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But I didn't know the persons. I didn't know them. Teresa McHenry either, I didn't know her by name.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. N, a moment ago in your testimony you said that between Temisoara and here in the Hague you had not given any statement, so that is not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was not a real statement. It was just a checking of what I had said. It's not a statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, in Belgrade in the Association of witnesses you made a supplementary additional statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not a statement and it was not given in the Association of Detainees.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It was in Belgrade on November 14th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in Belgrade but not in the Association of Detainees.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Allow me now, since you have recognised this statement, after it was shown to you, to ask you a few questions in this connection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not a statement, I must repeat. A statement is one thing; this is just a few words.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. N, will you please answer my questions, and what the document means is stated clearly on the document. Therefore, please, Mr. N, will you please confirm whether after that also, as on the first occasion, you signed the testimony in English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My statement? Yes, I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You had an interpreter during the interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you signed a certificate stating that this statement had been read out to you in the Serbian language and it is faithful to your knowledge and memory; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. N. Allow me now to go back to your previous statement. You have already said, but please confirm once again, that your first statement is much longer than the second one; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said once that it was not a statement. It was just confirming the first statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. N, will you please answer my question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have answered it, and I don't wish to answer any more questions that are not directly linked to this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please remind the witness that he is obliged to answer the questions put to him by the defence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually it is if he understands them, is it not? I do not think a witness should not answer a question. He should answer the questions. If he has not understood them, phrase them better so that he can understand what you are asking, because I think the whole problem arises from what you think he said here and over there. They are two places. He has been insisting that he did not make any statements in The Hague. It is possible he has made several statements outside here. So you take each of the statements and put them to him. If he says they are not statements, what are they then; ask him that. At least he was telling the prosecution what he knew about the matter. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you for your advice. I have just shown the witness his statement carrying his personal data, which he confirmed, and which he made on November 14th before Sabine Manke, interpreter, Miodrag Savic, and in the presence of Mrs Teresa McHenry, and which he signed carrying the certificate that the statement was read to him in the Serbian language and it corresponds best to his knowledge and recollection. He confirmed just now that he made this statement in Belgrade. So, your Honour, since we are dealing now with two statements made by the witness, allow me to ask him a few questions in that question. Mr. N, I will ask you with regard to facts linked to events you are familiar with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Ms Residovic, I think we can now rise and you can continue your cross-examination tomorrow morning. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Okay, your Honours. (4.00 pm)
